--- title: "Overview and workflow" subtitle: "The typed path from dataset to first-level fit, contrast, and group summary." jupyter: python3 execute: freeze: auto --- ## Follow the analysis `fmrimod` runs one typed workflow from data to group results. Every arrow below is a typed Python value, not a string or a hand-built matrix: ```text fmri_dataset -> fmri_lm(spec) -> contrast -> group ``` This page walks the first-level segment on a small example with a known injected effect; the [golden path](golden-path.qmd) carries the same workflow all the way into the group stage. ## Dataset An event table plus an acquisition grid, bound together in an `fmri_dataset`. ::: {#cf23cd7a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import pandas as pd import fmrimod as fm from fmrimod.spec import hrf from fmrimod.spec import compile as compile_spec from fmrimod.contrast import condition from fmrimod.simulate import simulate_bold events = pd.DataFrame({ "onset": np.arange(8, 210, 12.0), "stim_type": np.where(np.arange(17) % 2 == 0, "face", "scene"), "duration": 2.0, }) ``` ::: We use simulated data with a **known** face−scene effect of `2.0` in five of ten voxels. The point of working with simulated data here is that we know the right answer: a correct fit must return ≈ `2.0` in those voxels and ≈ `0` in the other five. ::: {#25f65484 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} spec = hrf("stim_type", basis="spmg1") ``` ::: Compile the event part of the public spec, resolve the authored hypothesis against public design provenance, then use the public simulator. The injected coefficient vector is normalized so that evaluating this exact contrast must return `2.0`; no column position is assumed. ::: {#92022023 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} sampling = fm.SamplingFrame(blocklens=220, TR=1.0) built, _ = compile_spec(spec, data=events, sampling_frame=sampling) design = np.asarray(built.design_matrix) hypothesis = condition("face", term="stim_type") - condition( "scene", term="stim_type" ) placeholder = fm.fmri_dataset( np.zeros((design.shape[0], 1)), tr=1.0, events=events ) weights = hypothesis.resolve( fm.fmri_lm(spec, placeholder).design_columns() )[: design.shape[1]] betas = np.zeros((design.shape[1], 10)) betas[:, :5] = 2.0 * weights[:, None] / (weights @ weights) bold = simulate_bold( design, betas, noise_sd=0.3, n_voxels=10, rng=np.random.default_rng(42), ) dataset = fm.fmri_dataset(bold, tr=1.0, events=events) ``` ::: ## Fit the specification The spec is a typed `hrf(...)` value — one HRF-convolved regressor per stimulus level. `fmri_lm` compiles it, adds the baseline, and returns an inspectable fit. ::: {#da3949b4 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fit = fm.fmri_lm(spec, dataset) fit # typed FmriLmResult — coefficients, residual df, solver config ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` FmriLm( n_coefficients=3, n_voxels=10, residual_df=217.0, config=FmriLmConfig(OLS), contrasts=[], ) ``` ::: ::: The realized design is readable from the fit — built for you, still inspectable. ::: {#ad5e90a3 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} list(fit.model.design_matrix(run=0).columns) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` ['stim_type_stim_type.face', 'stim_type_stim_type.scene', 'base_constant1_block_1'] ``` ::: ::: ## Name the contrast The scientific comparison names conditions, not column positions. ::: {#4a0c8c38 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} face_vs_scene = fit.contrast( hypothesis, name="face_vs_scene", ) pd.DataFrame({ "estimate": face_vs_scene.estimate.round(3), "t": face_vs_scene.stat.round(2), "p": face_vs_scene.p_value.round(4), }) # voxels 0–4 recover the injected ≈ 2.0; voxels 5–9 are null ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
estimate t p
0 1.805 9.53 0.0000
1 2.002 10.58 0.0000
2 2.218 11.84 0.0000
3 1.947 9.45 0.0000
4 1.836 10.08 0.0000
5 0.136 0.71 0.4796
6 0.195 0.94 0.3486
7 0.193 0.99 0.3241
8 0.072 0.36 0.7199
9 -0.179 -0.88 0.3797
``` ::: ::: The estimate returns the effect we injected. Recovering the planted value (not just *some* value) is the evidence that the design, the fit, and the contrast weights are all specified correctly. ## Continue to group analysis The final arrow — carrying these per-subject `ContrastResult` objects into a second-level (group) model to ask whether the effect holds across subjects — is shown end to end, with a check against Nilearn, on the **[golden path](golden-path.qmd)**. We stop at the first level here so each stage stays small enough to read; the golden path is the same workflow run without a break. ## Where to go next The same dataset-and-spec pattern carries through to the rest of the modeling stack: alternative GLM engines, AR whitening for temporally correlated noise, single-trial estimation, and ready-made benchmark datasets. Each is one option on the same `fmri_lm` call rather than a separate API to learn. ## Next - [The golden path](golden-path.qmd) — the whole workflow into group, with a parity check - [Linear model](linear-model.qmd) - [Contrasts](contrasts.qmd) - [Group analysis](group-analysis.qmd)
